Buttons.use: Runs an action. The variant says how prominent that action is on the page.
Copies a string to the clipboard and confirms the copy in place.
Groups related buttons, and becomes a single-choice segmented control when given `value` and `onChange`.
A button that opens a menu of actions.

Inputs.use: A password field with a reveal toggle and an optional copy affordance.
A password and its confirmation, sharing one reveal toggle.
A multi-line text field, optionally growing with its content.
One option turned on or off, applied when the form is submitted.
One choice among two to four mutually exclusive options.
One setting turned on or off, taking effect immediately.
One choice from a long or dynamic list; it gains a search field past eight options.
A Select preset with the health statuses as its options.
A text field that filters what is shown as it is typed into.
A variable-length list of fields the user adds rows to and removes rows from.
A value shown as text that becomes editable in place and saves through a mutation.
A drop area for attaching files, with a button for picking them instead.
A JSON editor with syntax highlighting and schema validation.

Forms.use: Lays a form out as a page or inside a tab, with its title, its fields and its action bar.
A titled group of fields inside a Form, owning the width of the label column.
One labelled field, with its help text, its error and its required marker.

Navigation.use: The application bar across the top: logo, tabs and the account actions.
The collapsible navigation rail down the side.
The path from the root of the application to the page being shown.
Switches between sibling views without leaving the page.
One view inside `Tabs`, carrying its own label.
react-router's `Routes`, reporting which route pattern matched.
Collects what those `Routes` report. Wrap the application in it once.
The pattern of the page being shown, such as `/nodes/:name/alerts`.
Applies the library's scrollbar styling to everything inside it.
The page for a user who is signed in but not allowed here.
The page for a route that does not exist.
The page for a request the server could not complete.
The full-page wait shown while authentication is still in progress.

Feedback.use: A condition that holds, shown for as long as it holds.
The outcome of an action that just completed. It dismisses itself.
Hosts the toasts. Wrap the application in it once.
Shows a toast from anywhere under the provider.
Turns a mutation's success or failure into a toast, including mutations that depend on another.
A fixed stack of dismissible notifications in one corner of the screen.
Interrupts the user for a decision that has to be made before anything else continues.
A panel sliding in from an edge for a task done alongside the page.
A short explanation attached to a field or a section, with an optional link out.
What a table or a list shows instead of rows while it is loading, when it failed, and when it is empty.

Data display.use: The data grid: sorting, selection, and virtualised rows.
The row a table shows in place of its body when it has none.
The screen for a resource list with nothing in it yet, carrying the action that creates the first one.
A bounded block of content, optionally selectable and optionally carrying a status.
A titled section the reader expands and collapses.
A short label marking a value, optionally removable.
Overlays a small status badge on whatever it wraps.
Text clamped to a number of lines, with the whole value in a tooltip.
A byte count written in the largest unit that keeps it readable.
A date in one of the library's formats, including relative to now.

Charts.use: Values compared across categories, as bars.
One or more series plotted over time.
A trend line small enough to sit inside a table row or a card.
Health across a time window as a single bar, with the alerts behind it.
A matrix of entities against time slots, each cell coloured by its value.
The legend for a chart, and the control over which series are shown.
Shares one legend, its colour set and its selection across several charts.
Reads and drives that shared legend state.
A stable id for one chart instance, for registering it with the legend.
Shares the selected time span across the charts under it.
Reads and sets that shared time span.
Barchart's own tooltip, for when the default needs replacing.
The frame of a hand-built chart tooltip.
The header of a hand-built chart tooltip.
The body of a hand-built chart tooltip.
One series line inside a hand-built chart tooltip.

Progress and loading.use: The spinner shown while something is on its way.
The sizes `Loader` accepts, as an object to index rather than a string to spell.
How far an operation of known length has got.
The same progress as a ring, where a bar does not fit.
Drives a multi-step flow: it renders the current step and moves between them.
The indicator showing the steps and which one the user is on.

Layout.use: The application frame: a header navigation slot above everything else.
The content area inside `Layout2`, with its summary, context and main-content regions.
Two panels side by side at a fixed ratio.
A frame with the navigation down the side instead of across the top.
The first frame: navbar, sidebar and content. `Layout2` supersedes it.
The styling primitive: spacing, colour and layout applied as props.
Children in a row or a column at one gap, optionally separated and optionally stacking when narrow.
Two children pushed to opposite ends of a row.
The spacing scale, for use inside a styled component.

Text and icons.use: Text at a chosen size and emphasis. Everything below is a preset of it.
Supporting text, in the secondary colour.
Text standing out from what surrounds it.
The title sitting above a chart.
An anchor carrying the link styling.
One of the library's icons, sized and coloured from the theme.
The question mark that carries an explanation in a tooltip.

Theme, values and helpers.use: Installs a theme. Wrap the application in it once.
A number written to ISO 80000-1: space-separated thousands, and enough decimals to keep two significant digits.
A date as `06 Oct`, for a long-range axis or a tight column.
The 24-hour `HH:mm` formatter the date components use.
The distance between two dates in months, days, hours or minutes.
